rows.path: motor output ↔ 7075 adapter (dowels, load sharing, + 3 × M4 friction) vs the drive limit (35.1)
rows.basis: bearing allowable 150 MPa (reverted from 240: cast A380-class σ_y ≈ 160 MPa with no bearing factor, ESTIMATE until the seller names the boss material; a steel or wrought 6061-T6 boss would justify ≈ 240). 3 × Ø4 × 4 mm on r 14.25: 2.40 kN each; dowel stiffness 41 kN/mm (Huth, Ø4 steel in 4 mm Al + 7 mm 7075); the first dowel takes k·δ before the others touch: δ 8 µm (H7/m6 spread, ISO 286) when the dowels are bonded (Loctite 638) into Ø4.1 adapter holes while seated in the motor (the adapter's hole positions drop out) → 93 N·m; dry in jig-bored holes δ ≈ 40 µm (± 0.02 true position each side, ESTIMATE) → 56 N·m (the review's ≈ 55 N·m); equal sharing 103 N·m. + 3 × M4 × 10 csk at 2.0 kN, μ 0.15, metal on metal (no creep): 13 N·m (strip of 2.65 mm effective M4 in the cast boss ≈ 3.9 kN). Dowel shear 242 N·m (ISO 8734). Criterion: stall is a fault, checked at a yield-level bearing allowable at ≥ 1.0× (as bolts ≤ proof); the 7075 adapter side is 7 mm deep. The 140 N bump puts up to 0 N·m on the roll output (0.00× this capacity): below the stall only if the actuator backdrives at its current limit (open: backdrive torque, seller / bench)
